answer: Delayed-Release Namespace Claim. Each new identity must publish a claim into a shared namespace that only becomes actionable at dawn of a later epoch, and the claim is anchored to a basalt ledger checkpoint that cannot be rewritten. Any identity impersonating an existing one forces its claim onto the same jetty slot, triggering a collision fee that scales with how many prior claims share the target. An attacker controlling N identities pays the collision fee N times over per target, so crowding identifiers costs superlinearly while honest single claims stay cheap.
